low_power_modes_summary.n_a_at_protocol_layer: MODBUS is an application-layer (OSI level 7) protocol — it has no built-in low-power state, sleep/wake handshake, or power-management exchange.
low_power_modes_summary.implementation_strategies: Devices implementing MODBUS commonly gate the UART / Ethernet PHY clock between transactions, and the host CPU may sleep until the underlying transport raises an end-of-frame or socket-receive interrupt. None of this is required or specified by Modbus.org.
low_power_modes_summary.no_explicit_sleep_command: There is no MODBUS function code that places the server into a low-power state. Some vendors define User-Defined-range function codes (65..72 / 100..110) for proprietary sleep/wake; these are not interoperable across vendors.

fields.notes: Any low-power behavior is a property of the implementing silicon and firmware, not of the MODBUS protocol itself. Power-domain partitioning, isolation cells, retention, and UPF are concerns at the IP-integration layer and are out of scope for this Modbus.org document.
